---
title: "Tetrahedral Mesh Quality"
---

`scgsim.palace.check_mesh_quality()` reads a solver-bound Gmsh MSH 2.2 ASCII
file without starting Gmsh or Palace. It returns an immutable
`MeshQualityReport` for the linear four-node tetrahedra that are actually in
that file. This is a diagnostic reading surface, not a mesh repair step and not
a scientific acceptance gate.

## Input and ownership

The reader accepts only MSH 2.2 ASCII files and preserves node and element IDs,
element order, original binary64 coordinates, raw tag order, and
dimension-qualified physical names. Other element types are counted but are
not silently reinterpreted as linear tetrahedra. Known public MSH element codes
must have their standard node arity; future unknown codes remain counted as
unknown rather than acquiring a guessed dimension. Missing node references and
nonfinite coordinates stay attached to their element IDs as unavailable
records; malformed sections and duplicate IDs fail closed.

Reading is sequential. The report binds the parsed byte count, SHA-256, and
before/after file identity, and does not retain an open file or reread the mesh
for later summaries, export, or visualization. A report owns read-only compact
arrays. Returned dictionaries and Plotly figures are detached presentation
objects and cannot mutate retained measurements.

## Numerical meaning

For authored tetrahedron vertices \(p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3\), the edge matrix is

\[
B = [p_1-p_0\; p_2-p_0\; p_3-p_0].
\]

The signed mesh-unit volume is \(\det(B)/6\); the reported volume magnitude is
\(|\det(B)|/6\). Orientation and magnitude are separate: a positive,
negative, or exact-zero orientation is never inferred from a rounded absolute
volume.

The fast orientation path first applies one exactly reversible power-of-two
scale to all twelve coordinates of the element, before subtraction. It uses a
Shewchuk-style determinant error bound \(E=(7+56u)uP\), with binary64 unit
roundoff \(u=2^{-53}\) and \(P\) formed in the matching triple-product order,
only for the sign decision. A bound
that is inconclusive, a scale that loses a finite nonzero value, or a
representation-boundary ambiguity takes the exact fallback based on
`float.as_integer_ratio()` values from the original coordinates. Nonfinite
coordinates remain locatable but numerically unavailable. The report
retains the determinant estimate, absolute sign bound, and the selected
method. The exact fallback computes mesh-unit and optional SI volume
independently before either result is rounded to binary64, so mesh and SI
underflow or overflow remain distinct statuses rather than false zero or
infinity.

The condition metric uses

\[
J = B W^{-1},\qquad
W = \begin{bmatrix}
1 & 1/2 & 1/2 \\
0 & \sqrt{3}/2 & \sqrt{3}/6 \\
0 & 0 & \sqrt{2/3}
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad \kappa(J)=\sigma_{max}/\sigma_{min}.
\]

A regular reference tetrahedron therefore has \(\kappa=1\). Exact zero
determinants are singular. A nonzero exact determinant whose smallest singular
value is below the numerical-resolution threshold is reported as numerically
unresolved, not relabeled geometrically singular.
The threshold is \(\sigma_{min}\leq3\epsilon\sigma_{max}\), with binary64
spacing \(\epsilon=2^{-52}\). It is a reporting status, not a scientific
quality gate.

## Units, summaries, and ranking

`length_scale_m` is optional. Without it, mesh-unit volume is available and SI
volume is explicitly unavailable. Palace simulation wrappers pass their
existing micrometre model scale (`1e-6`) after a mesh has been built. A direct
call may supply another finite positive scale but does not infer one from the
file.

Summaries keep available values, exact singularities, numerical-resolution
failures, missing nodes, nonfinite coordinates, and representation failures in
separate counts. Statistics and worst-element ranks use only values whose
status makes them comparable. Condition-number ranking places exact
singularities first, then finite values in descending order; volume ranking is
ascending. Element ID breaks ties deterministically. These ranks describe the
selected diagnostic metric only and do not impose a pass/fail threshold.

`show_summary()` and `show_worst_elements()` provide text displays.
`show_elements()` imports Plotly lazily and draws the six authored edges for
each selected tetrahedron as lines and its four vertices once as markers, with
`aspectmode="data"`. Degenerate vertices remain
visible without rewriting coordinates or inflating a tiny nonzero dimension.
Unknown requested element IDs fail instead of being dropped.

These inert coordinate sets illustrate three distinct outcomes; they are not
executed by the documentation build and do not define acceptance thresholds:

```python
# p0, p1, p2, p3 in authored mesh units
regular = ((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0.5, 3**0.5 / 2, 0),
           (0.5, 3**0.5 / 6, (2 / 3)**0.5))
coplanar = ((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (1, 1, 0))
thin_nonzero = ((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (0, 0, 2**-100))
```

The regular set uses the documented reference matrix and has
\(\kappa(J)=1\). The coplanar set is exactly singular. The thin set has a
nonzero orientation and volume but a large condition number; the report keeps
those facts separate.

## Serialization and limitations

`to_dict()` returns detached plain containers. `save_json()` streams the same
schema to an exclusively created output file and refuses to overwrite the mesh
itself. Nonfinite or unavailable numerical values are serialized as `null` with
an explicit reason; JSON never contains `NaN` or `Infinity` tokens.

This V1 surface does not reorder tetrahedra to match solver orientation, repair
connectivity, evaluate higher-order tetrahedra, infer solver-side acceptance,
or prove convergence. It reads the stored mesh exactly once and reports its
own numerical evidence.

The numerical design follows Shewchuk's
[adaptive-predicate guidance](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake/robust.html) for
sign decisions and uses NumPy's documented
[SVD rank-resolution model](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.linalg.matrix_rank.html)
only as a numerical-resolution indicator. The
[MFEM mesh implementation](https://docs.mfem.org/4.9/mesh_8cpp_source.html) may
reorder elements in its own workflow; that does not redefine the orientation
of the original MSH connectivity inspected here.
